findings.title: Reject non-passing probe verdicts
findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
findings.originalBody:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-passing probe verdicts**

When the probe produces valid JSON but any A–D assertion is `FAIL` or remains `UNOBSERVED`, `Finish()` can still exit 0 because `firstError` is empty, and this block checks only cleanup before marking the stage `PASSED`; the final runner also exits 0 whenever `failure` is unset. This lets a failed or partial observation look successful to callers even though the receipt embeds a non-passing status. Require `observation["status"] == "OBSERVATION_COMPLETE"` before marking the stage passed, or otherwise propagate the verdict to the runner exit code.

findings.title: Require the comparison sample to be post-cancellation
findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
findings.originalBody:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the comparison sample to be post-cancellation**

If startup cancellation is delayed until after the first natural Canvas callback, that still-bound callback can satisfy C because the predicate checks only geometry, supported size, and a newer safe-area version; a later cancellation can then independently satisfy D. C would therefore report `PASS` without proving the advertised first-layout-versus-post-cancellation transition. Restrict the qualifying natural sample to the cancelled, unbound, unsubscribed state (and the expected released gate), rather than relying on the final snapshot.
